content:
This passage is from Homer's "Iliad," Book 19, lines 184-195. Here is the translation:

"The lord of men, Agamemnon, answered him:
‘I am pleased to hear, Laertes' son, your words;
For you have spoken all under adequate circumstances, and listed them.
I myself am willing to swear to it, my heart compels me,
And I will not swear falsely before a god. But let Achilles
Delay here, though eager for war:
And let all the rest of us remain assembled, until the gifts
Are brought from my tent, and we can swear a solemn oath.
To you, yourself, I give this injunction and command:
Choose the best young men of all Achaeans,
And take the gifts from my ship, all those we promised
To give to Achilles yesterday, and lead along the women.
But let Talthybius quickly prepare within the wide camp of the Achaeans
A boar to sacrifice to Zeus and to the Sun.'”
